name: Eduardo Avaroa Andean Fauna National Reserve
story: Eduardo Avaroa Andean Fauna National Reserve covers 714,745 hectares of southwestern Bolivia, featuring mountainous, desert-like landscapes and high-altitude lakes. Established in December 1973, it is home to vicuñas, pumas, and three flamingo species.
matters: The reserve protects an extreme environment and species adapted to high altitudes, serving as an important habitat for birds and part of the larger Los Lípez Ramsar site.
